newsitem.title: INDONESIA: BNI share issue said almost 350 pct oversubscribed.
newsitem.headline: BNI share issue said almost 350 pct oversubscribed.

text.p: PT Bank Negara Indonesia's (BNI) initial public offering has been oversubscribed almost 350 percent, with foreign investors accounting a large number of orders, the Jakarta Post reported on Saturday.

The newspaper quoted Agus Projosasmito, president of lead underwriter PT Danareksa Sekuritas, as saying on Friday that there were 4.84 billion orders for the 1.08 billion shares, or 25 percent of the state-owned bank's capital, on offer.
"We therefore have to reduce the allotment to foreign investors to give more opportunity to domestic investors," Projosasmito told reporters.
The report said foreign investors subscribed to 2.88 billion shares and domestic investors to 1.96 billion shares.
Projosasmito said the team of 79 underwriters had decided to reduce the foreign allotment of the total offering from 49 percent, the maximum allowed by capital market regulations, to 43.06 percent.
"By this, we can give local retail investors more opportunity to get BNI shares," he said.

The report said 786,267 of the 787,665 subscription forms had come from local investors and 617,693 of the local investors had applied for only one lot of 500 shares. Only 425,451 lots have been allocated for local retail investors.
It said a lottery was held on November 13 to distribute the available stocks to local retail investors.
The allocation system has been recently criticised by underwriters and investors who said procedures have been violated by selling fixed-allotment shares to wealthy individuals.
The government hopes to raise 922.25 billion rupiah from the issue.
While the share price has been set at 850 rupiah (36 cents), brokers have said this month were being traded at a premium of 125 to 150 rupiah on the grey market.
The BNI shares will be listed on November 25.
